__comment: SEED / test-grade G1 spec corpus carrying UNBOUNDED SENTINELS (po-av01j.25). The call-arg mechanism is value-aware: `unbounded_sentinels` lists the values of an API's own timeout argument that mean NO bound, so a resolved sentinel violates (citing the value and how it was resolved) instead of crediting a bound. Which values carry that meaning is library knowledge and therefore lives here, never in propagation. PRODUCTION corpus authoring rides the LLM factory and is HITL - these entries exist so the e2e test exercises real verdicts at identities pyindex actually emits, nothing more.

apis.rationale: SEED RC-019: requests.get blocks until the response completes; the bound is the per-call timeout= argument. requests documents timeout=None as 'wait forever', so the argument being PRESENT is not the question - its value is.
SEED RC-019: same surface as requests.get; timeout=None blocks forever

SEED RC-019: settimeout configures the socket rather than performing I/O, and both of its sentinels are documented: None restores blocking mode (no bound) and 0 selects non-blocking mode (not a bound either)
